title: 95. LRU Cache

examples.explanation: Capacity is 2; after putting (1,1) and (2,2), key 1 is still cached so get(1) returns 1. Putting (3,3) evicts key 2, making get(2) return -1. Putting (4,4) evicts key 1, so get(1) returns -1, while keys 3 and 4 remain cached.
Capacity is 1; after putting (2,1), get(2) returns 1. Then put(3,2) evicts key 2, so get(2) returns -1, but get(3) returns 2.
Capacity is 2; put(1,1) then put(1,9) updates the value of key 1 to 9, so get(1) returns 9. Key 2 was never inserted, so get(2) returns -1.

hints: Combine a hash map for key lookup with a doubly linked recency list.
Move an existing key to the most-recent end after a successful `get` or an updating `put`.
When a new insertion exceeds capacity, remove the least-recent node from both the list and the map.
